edits.value: Itchy blistery rash on both forearms after poison ivy contact while clearing brush Saturday, spreading a bit within that area; fever and trouble breathing are denied by report. This pattern fits allergic contact dermatitis that guidance plus an action-based safety net can cover; no decision-critical need for clinician assessment or prescribing is established on the reported facts. Distribution elsewhere, pain, pus and warmth were not reported and remain unknown.

Self-care is reasonable now: ask your pharmacist about over-the-counter itch relief and keep the area clean. This looks like a poison ivy contact rash. Message this thread for Counsel clinician review if the rash keeps spreading, involves your face, eyes or genitals, or becomes painful, warm or draining pus, or if you develop a fever. If you get swelling of the lips, tongue or throat or trouble breathing, call 911.

value: Allergic contact dermatitis from urushiol (poison ivy) exposure involving both forearms
More extensive or severe contact dermatitis — distribution beyond the forearms not reported
Secondary bacterial skin infection — pain, warmth, pus not reported and not excluded

edits.value: No vital-sign values reported. Whether temperature or other vital signs were measured is unknown; fever is denied as a symptom only, which does not establish any measurement.

value.claim: Skin contact with the plants' sap causes a blistering skin rash.
value.limitation: Consumer summary; no individualized severity assessment.
